answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies works best through proof-of-work plus staked identity. Each agent must burn real compute to register, and every action carries a bond locked on-ledger. A new identity therefore cannot be assembled like cheap timber: forging thousands of fake agents multiplies both compute cost and staked capital, and a single slash destroys the whole bond. Honest agents act as a bridge between reputations, so a fresh address ranks near the zenith of cost but the bottom of trust, and pays full price until peers attest it.
